sections.sectionTitle: Paper 1 & Paper 2: Theory and Composition & History/Literature

topics.title: Rudiments, Elementary Harmony, Composition, and Form/Analysis

subtopics.content: Notation, Western scales, African modes, keys, time signatures, intervals, transcription, transposition, musical terms/signs/ornaments, primary/secondary triads, cadences, non-harmonic tones, modulations, SATB harmony, two-part counterpoint, melodic continuation, text setting, simple/extended/African forms, and analysis of prescribed set-works
subtopics.objective: Master staff/clef notation, Western diatonic/chromatic scales, African 5/6/7-tone modes, key signatures, intervals, transcription, and transposition[cite: 497]; harmonize melodies using primary/secondary triads, inversions, cadences, non-harmonic tones, modulations, and 4-part SATB / 2-part counterpoint[cite: 497, 498]; compose 12-16 bar melodies and set English text to music[cite: 498]; analyze musical forms (binary, ternary, rondo, sonata, call and response) and set-works by Haydn, Pappoe-Thompson, Dvorak, Akin Euba, J.S. Bach, Laz Ekwueme, Verdi, Mereku, Schubert, and Ayo Bankole[cite: 498, 499].

topics.title: History and Literature of Music (Western, African, Popular, and Black Diaspora)

subtopics.content: Biographies and achievements of Traditional African musicians, Popular African musicians (Highlife, Afrobeat, Juju, Fuji, Waka, Afro-Pop, Afro-Reggae, Hip-Hop), Contemporary African Art musicians, Western music historical periods (Medieval, Renaissance, Baroque, Classical, Romantic, 20th Century), Black Music in the Diaspora (Jazz, Blues, Reggae, Calypso), and traditional African music roles/instruments/dances
subtopics.objective: Examine contributions of traditional African musicians (Dan Maraya, Hubert Ogunde, Mamman Shata, Kakraba Lobi)[cite: 502]; evaluate popular African genres and artists (Fela Kuti, King Sunny Ade, E.T. Mensah, Tuface Idibia)[cite: 502, 503]; trace African art music pioneers (Fela Sowande, Ephraim Amu, J.H.K. Nketia)[cite: 503]; survey Western eras and major composers (Palestrina, Bach, Handel, Mozart, Beethoven, Chopin, Stravinsky)[cite: 503, 504]; study Black Diaspora genres (Spirituals, Jazz, Blues, Reggae)[cite: 504]; analyze traditional African instruments, structural characteristics, song categories, and traditional dances (Adowa, Fontomfrom, Bata, Atilogwu)[cite: 504, 505].

subtopics.content: Rhythmic dictation, melody writing, two-part ear training, chord identification, cadence recognition, key modulation identification, theme description, sight-reading, technical exercises, scales/arpeggios, and solo performance on voice or chosen instrument (Pianoforte, Violin, Wind instruments)
subtopics.objective: Transcribe rhythms, melodies, and two-part phrases from sound dictation[cite: 499, 500]; identify chords, cadences, modulations, and musical themes aurally[cite: 500]; perform technical exercises, scales, arpeggios, sight-reading, and prescribed solo works on voice, keyboard, violin, or wind instruments (recorder, atenteben, flute, trumpet, alto-saxophone)[cite: 496, 501, 506, 508, 509, 510, 511, 512].
